summary: extrahtml 0.1.1 is a lure that pulls an unpinned lookalike dependency and fetches mutable content at install time
details: The extrahtml 0.1.1 sdist ships no implementation of the library it advertises. The README documents RequestsEngine, SeleniumEngine and PlaywrightEngine under `from extrahtml import...`, but the tarball contains only `extrahtml.egg-info/` metadata, an empty `top_level.txt`, and `setup.py` — no `extrahtml` package source. The only install-time effects are (1) resolving `install_requires = ["requests>=2.28.0", "parseyaml>=1.2.0", "fake-useragent>=1.4.0"]` plus `pyproject [build-system] requires parseyaml>=1.2.0`, which pulls `parseyaml`, a non-mainstream lookalike of PyYAML whose author controls whatever code is published under that name, and (2) `setup.py` performing a network GET to `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/optima1236/parsetxt/refs/heads/main/README.md` and passing the response body to `parseyaml.safe_load` during `pip install`. The URL points at the mutable `refs/heads/main` of a personal GitHub repository owned by the same author, so the content fed into the author-controlled parser can change at any time after publish. The combination of a hollow package, a lookalike build/runtime dependency, and install-time fetching of unpinned content from a personal GitHub branch into an author-controlled parser is a dropper-lure shape: installing extrahtml resolves and executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's host, with no legitimate functionality shipped by the package itself.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
